subsystems.name: Reflector film
subsystems.role: a large, ultra-light mirror that redirects sunlight.

subsystems.name: Deployment structure
subsystems.role: unfurls and holds the film flat in space.

subsystems.name: Attitude control and pointing
subsystems.role: keeps the mirror oriented so reflected light hits the target footprint.

subsystems.name: Power and avionics
subsystems.role: runs the spacecraft and communicates with the ground.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: plans the beam footprint, commands the constellation and coordinates with aviation and astronomers.

buildSteps.title: Design the orbit and coverage
buildSteps.detail: Choose an altitude and phasing that lets a mirror pass over the target region at night, and calculate the spot size and brightness on the ground.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the reflector film
buildSteps.detail: Deposit a thin aluminium layer onto a polymer sheet, cut it to shape, and add tensioning points and rip-stop lines.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Pack the folded film, deployment booms, control systems, power and communication into a launch fairing.

buildSteps.title: Launch and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Rocket the spacecraft to orbit, then inflate or extend the booms to pull the film flat and rigid.

buildSteps.title: Commission and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Use star trackers and ground lasers to align the mirror, then measure the actual beam footprint and intensity on the ground.

buildSteps.title: Operate as a constellation
buildSteps.detail: Launch multiple mirrors and phase them so at least one covers the service area at any time, with software coordinating pointing.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and dispose
buildSteps.detail: Monitor degradation from ultraviolet light and micrometeoroids, and at end of life lower the orbit or use a drag sail so the mirror burns up.

prerequisites.why: demonstrated at 20-metre scale in the 1990s, but not yet at the hundreds-of-metres scale needed for useful illumination.
satellites already point instruments to arcsecond accuracy, which is enough to steer a reflected beam.
polymer films degrade in ultraviolet light and atomic oxygen; space-rated coatings exist but are not proven for decades.

prerequisites.tech: Orbital debris mitigation and end-of-life disposal
prerequisites.why: guidelines exist, but large fragile mirrors could create debris if they break up.

prerequisites.tech: International coordination on light pollution and aviation safety
prerequisites.why: no framework yet governs who may illuminate the night sky and at what brightness.

pathway.unlocks: proof that a film reflector can deploy and point.

pathway.milestone: a single large reflector in low Earth orbit that brightens a small area for minutes
pathway.unlocks: real measurements of beam shaping and ecological effects.

pathway.milestone: a constellation of a few mirrors giving intermittent coverage of a city or disaster zone
pathway.unlocks: operational use for emergency response and night-time construction.

pathway.milestone: scaled-up fleets offering persistent illumination over large regions
pathway.unlocks: agricultural and industrial applications, if regulation and astronomy protection are settled.
